meta.title: Unannounced DRO departure — custody loss and recovery (SIMULATED)
meta.epoch_choice_rationale: Window 2026-02-23 .. 2026-03-01 UTC (6 days, hourly frames) inside the cached DE440s/Horizons span. Scanning the span with the real visibility model: SIM-DRO-01 stays within ~12 deg of the Moon on the sky, so under the phase-dependent lunar-glare exclusion (3 deg at new Moon to 15 deg at full Moon) the nine ground sites can only track it on the nights of Feb 23-25 (Moon 33-60 % illuminated, exclusion 7-10 deg, object 10-11 deg from the Moon) and are blind from Feb 25 ~11 UTC through full Moon (Mar 3). The burn is placed 30 min after the last pre-burn ground tracklet so that exactly one post-burn ground observation catches the anomaly before the glare closes the window; the loss is therefore computed, not scripted. Known fragility: that tracklet clears the assumed phase-dependent glare cone by only ~0.1 deg, so a different glare parameterisation or a 30-min epoch shift leaves no post-burn ground observation and the builder raises instead of inventing a detection.
meta.burn_rationale: 30 m/s (assumed, inside the 20-40 m/s class) at 2026-02-25T08:30Z. Direction: of 256 Fibonacci-sampled 30 m/s burn directions propagated with the reachability engine, the one whose coasting arc passes closest to the Earth-Moon L1 point (~510 km at +41.5 h vs ~4 200 km for the unperturbed DRO). The notional actor's intent is never inferred.
assumptions: All sensors are notional (assumed representative specs); astrometric noise 1 arcsec (1-sigma, isotropic on-sky).
Routine custody: one ground tracklet every 2 h when any site can see the object; space observers are allocated to the libration-point objects until the tasker escalates.

Filter: UKF with DE440s Earth+Moon+Sun+SRP dynamics, process-noise PSD 1e-18 km^2/s^3; the t0 prior (5 km / 0.2 m/s, 1-sigma) stands for the catalogue covariance of an object that has been under custody for weeks (the 20 km / 2 m/s acquisition prior would drift past 100 km in the 8-h gaps between ground sites); after a gross NIS exceedance the prior is re-opened for an impulsive dv of sigma 25 m/s at an unknown epoch in the last gap (must bound the burn class).
Custody thresholds on the particle-cloud RSS position sigma: < 100 km CUSTODY, 100-1000 km DEGRADED, > 1000 km LOST.

Reachability: assumed 100 m/s planning budget, 168 h horizon, impulsive burns on a Fibonacci sphere x absolute magnitude ladder x burn epochs spanning the detection gap; fractions are fractions of sampled (direction, epoch) rays.

Tasking: greedy scheduler (trace gain for routine custody, log-det information gain for the escalation because re-acquisition must resolve range and velocity, not just plane-of-sky position) with the FOV acquisition model; every tasked look is verified against the SIMULATED truth (visibility model + mosaic of fields around the reachable-set centroid), never assumed; the scheduler's acquisition model and the verification share one search budget of 25 fields per 60-min slot (no explicit slew/exposure timeline); one slot of re-planning latency between the loss declaration and the first tasked look.

Ground-blind attribution: per hourly frame only the sites that are available (astronomical night, object above the minimum elevation) are asked why they are blocked; frames where no site is available are reported as 'no_site_available', not as glare.
Force model has no lunar gravity field or planetary perturbations beyond the Sun; light-time and aberration are not modelled.
meta.disclaimer: SIMULATED scenario. Every object, event and burn is notional and attributed to a 'notional actor' or 'notional allied operator'; no real country, operator or spacecraft is implicated. Sensor specifications are assumed representative values. This is a defensive awareness and traffic-safety product: reachability and tasking describe where an object could be and where to look, never intent or engagement.
build_log: declared at 2026-02-25T10:00:00Z (NIS 6178, sensor siding_spring), latency 1.50 h
custody lost (sigma > 1000 km) at 2026-02-25T19:00:00Z; sigma at detection 104 km
tasker: 88 protagonist assignments in segment B (search_tiles=25, gain=logdet)
re-acquisition: OK by geo_west,geo_east,l1_halo_obs,dro_obs,nrho_obs (5 looks verified), 38 space tracklets

extra_event_kinds.maneuver: SIMULATED-truth marker of the burn itself (never visible to the operator at that instant)

regions.name: L1 gateway
regions.why_it_matters: Every low-energy transfer between the Earth realm and the lunar realm threads the L1 neck; an object that can reach it can reach the Moon-Earth corridor and the lunar vicinity.

regions.name: L2 gateway
regions.why_it_matters: The L2 neck is the doorway to translunar space and the home of far-side relays and halo/NRHO traffic; it is also the hardest region to observe from Earth (behind the Moon, lunar glare).

regions.name: NRHO corridor (9:2)
regions.why_it_matters: The 9:2 NRHO is the staging/relay corridor (Gateway class); an unidentified object entering the tube is a conjunction-screening and traffic-safety concern for the notional allied relay.

regions.name: Lunar south-pole approach
regions.why_it_matters: South-pole landers, relays and the NRHO perilune passes all live here; it is the busiest lunar approach volume of the coming decade and sits in the Earth-facing/far-side limb geometry that ground sensors struggle with.

regions.name: Low lunar orbit shell
regions.why_it_matters: The shell occupied by science orbiters and descent/ascent arcs; entry means a close lunar approach and a conjunction-screening obligation.

regions.name: Low lunar orbit (inner, < 500 km)
regions.why_it_matters: Where most active lunar orbiters fly; the tightest conjunction-screening volume.

regions.name: GEO belt return
regions.why_it_matters: An xGEO object dropping back toward the GEO belt is the highest-consequence Earth-orbit safety case: it crosses the most valuable orbital regime at km/s relative speeds and is hard to track until it is close.

regions.name: Exterior-realm excursion (beyond the L2 neck)
regions.why_it_matters: Beyond ~500 000 km the object is outside the volume Moon-pointed sensors search; whether it later escapes or swings back, custody is lost unless the network is re-tasked outward.

regions.name: Lunar impact
regions.why_it_matters: Pure safety: an impacting trajectory ends custody and may endanger surface assets.

events.text: SIM-DRO-01 under routine custody: ground-network tracklets every 2 h when a site can see it (Moon 33 % illuminated, object 6.2 deg from the Moon). Prior 1-sigma 5 km / 0.2 m/s; the space observers are allocated to the other catalogued SIMULATED objects.

[SIMULATED truth] notional actor performs an unannounced 30 m/s burn on SIM-DRO-01 (RTN -29.6/+5.0/-1.3 m/s, moon-centred). Not visible to the operator at this instant.

MANEUVER DETECTED on SIM-DRO-01: siding_spring tracklet is 97" off the predicted position (NIS 6178 vs family-wise threshold 18.3 at alpha = 0.01). Filter covariance re-opened for an unknown impulsive dv (sigma 25 m/s over the 2.0 h gap).

CUSTODY DEGRADED on SIM-DRO-01: particle-cloud sigma_pos 102 km > 100 km (a single post-burn angles-only tracklet cannot resolve the dv). Ground network blind from 2026-02-25T11:00:00Z: no ground site has the object above its elevation limit at night (daylight or below the horizon everywhere) (Moon 61 % illuminated, object 10.1 deg from it, glare exclusion 10.3 deg). From 2026-02-25T15:00:00Z the sites that do have it up at night (diego_garcia) are blocked by lunar glare alone. Uncertainty growing at ~2160 km/day.

REACHABILITY (awareness only): from the last good state with an assumed 100 m/s budget over 168 h, SIM-DRO-01 could enter: L1 gateway: on the unperturbed path (first entry +34 h with no burn; earliest +29 h with a burn); L2 gateway: 28 % of sampled rays, earliest +108 h, >= 11 m/s. The corridor of the notional allied relay (SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01, 9:2 NRHO) is not reached by any of the 1728 sampled rays within this budget and horizon (at or below the sampling resolution: a marginal hit at the budget limit cannot be excluded). Recommendation: increased custody on the object and conjunction screening for the relay; no closer approach is implied.

# Analyst brief — Unannounced DRO departure — custody loss and recovery (SIMULATED)

**Scenario window:** 2026-02-23T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z (UTC). **Object of interest:** SIM-DRO-01, a SIMULATED medium-size spacecraft of a notional actor in a distant retrograde orbit (DRO) about the Moon. **Asset of concern:** SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01, a SIMULATED relay of a notional allied operator in the 9:2 NRHO.

## Bottom line up front
- At 2026-02-25T10:00:00Z SELENE detected an unannounced maneuver by SIM-DRO-01: a single ground tracklet from siding_spring was 97 arcsec off the predicted position (normalised innovation squared, NIS, 6,178 against a threshold of 18.3), 1.5 h after the burn.
- The ground network then went blind: in 79 of the 86 blind hours after the detection every site that had the object up at night was stopped by lunar glare (the object was too close to the bright Moon on the sky), and in the other 7 hours no site had it above its elevation limit at night at all. Custody was declared LOST at 2026-02-25T19:00:00Z when the position uncertainty exceeded 1,000 km (peak 1,053 km); at that instant the blocker was lunar glare at sutherland.
- The tasker redirected geo_west, geo_east, l1_halo_obs, dro_obs and nrho_obs to the reachable-set centroid; the object was re-acquired at 2026-02-25T20:00:00Z and custody was regained at 2026-02-25T20:00:00Z (1.0 h after the loss).
- The maneuver is characterised as a 30.02 ± 0.03 m/s impulsive burn at 2026-02-25T08:30:45Z ± 53 s (radial (inward)); against the SIMULATED truth of 30.0 m/s the magnitude error is 0.1 % and the direction error 0.1°.
- Under the assumed 100 m/s budget the relay's NRHO corridor is not reached by any of the 1728 sampled rays within 168 h — a result at or below the sampling resolution, so a marginal entry at the budget limit cannot be excluded; recommendation: keep elevated custody on SIM-DRO-01 and run conjunction screening for SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01. No intent is inferred.

## Timeline (UTC)
- `2026-02-23T00:00:00Z` **custody_nominal** — SIM-DRO-01 under routine custody: ground-network tracklets every 2 h when a site can see it (Moon 33 % illuminated, object 6.2 deg from the Moon). Prior 1-sigma 5 km / 0.2 m/s; the space observers are allocated to the other catalogued SIMULATED objects.
- `2026-02-25T08:30:00Z` **maneuver** — [SIMULATED truth] notional actor performs an unannounced 30 m/s burn on SIM-DRO-01 (RTN -29.6/+5.0/-1.3 m/s, moon-centred). Not visible to the operator at this instant.
- `2026-02-25T10:00:00Z` **maneuver_detected** — MANEUVER DETECTED on SIM-DRO-01: siding_spring tracklet is 97" off the predicted position (NIS 6178 vs family-wise threshold 18.3 at alpha = 0.01). Filter covariance re-opened for an unknown impulsive dv (sigma 25 m/s over the 2.0 h gap).
- `2026-02-25T10:00:00Z` **custody_degraded** — CUSTODY DEGRADED on SIM-DRO-01: particle-cloud sigma_pos 102 km > 100 km (a single post-burn angles-only tracklet cannot resolve the dv). Ground network blind from 2026-02-25T11:00:00Z: no ground site has the object above its elevation limit at night (daylight or below the horizon everywhere) (Moon 61 % illuminated, object 10.1 deg from it, glare exclusion 10.3 deg). From 2026-02-25T15:00:00Z the sites that do have it up at night (diego_garcia) are blocked by lunar glare alone. Uncertainty growing at ~2160 km/day.
- `2026-02-25T10:00:00Z` **reachability_alert** — REACHABILITY (awareness only): from the last good state with an assumed 100 m/s budget over 168 h, SIM-DRO-01 could enter: L1 gateway: on the unperturbed path (first entry +34 h with no burn; earliest +29 h with a burn); L2 gateway: 28 % of sampled rays, earliest +108 h, >= 11 m/s. The corridor of the notional allied relay (SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01, 9:2 NRHO) is not reached by any of the 1728 sampled rays within this budget and horizon (at or below the sampling resolution: a marginal hit at the budget limit cannot be excluded). Recommendation: increased custody on the object and conjunction screening for the relay; no closer approach is implied.
- `2026-02-25T19:00:00Z` **custody_lost** — CUSTODY LOST on SIM-DRO-01: particle-cloud sigma_pos 1053 km > 1000 km with no observation since 2026-02-25T10:00:00Z. Ground: every site that has the object up at night (sutherland) is blocked by lunar glare (object inside the phase-dependent Moon exclusion cone) (dominant reason 'moon_exclusion'). Escalating to the space network.
- `2026-02-25T20:00:00Z` **tasking_update** — SELENE tasker redirects 5 space sensor(s) to SIM-DRO-01, boresights at the reachable-set centroid (primary geo_west: RA 81.59 deg, Dec +28.33 deg): geo_west (1 of 1 field(s) of 3 deg needed for the p90 spread 0.55 deg, range 328,193 km, mag 16.9); geo_east (1 of 1 field(s) of 3 deg needed for the p90 spread 0.54 deg, range 330,367 km, mag 17.3); l1_halo_obs (25 of 73 field(s) of 2 deg needed for the p90 spread 8.49 deg, range 18,518 km, mag 13.3); dro_obs (13 of 13 field(s) of 2 deg needed for the p90 spread 3.47 deg, range 52,383 km, mag 12.4); nrho_obs (4 of 4 field(s) of 2 deg needed for the p90 spread 1.79 deg, range 99,261 km, mag 16.4). Not tasked: l2_halo_obs (sun_exclusion). Scheduler: greedy logdet gain, FOV acquisition model with a search budget of 25 fields per slot, priority 3 on SIM-DRO-01.
- `2026-02-25T20:00:00Z` **observation** — RE-ACQUIRED SIM-DRO-01: geo_west truth 0.20 deg from boresight (mosaic radius 1.50 deg); geo_east truth 0.22 deg from boresight (mosaic radius 1.50 deg); l1_halo_obs truth 2.51 deg from boresight (mosaic radius 5.00 deg); dro_obs truth 1.06 deg from boresight (mosaic radius 3.47 deg); nrho_obs truth 0.55 deg from boresight (mosaic radius 1.79 deg). Follow-up tracklets per the tasker's plan every 2 h.
- `2026-02-25T20:00:00Z` **custody_regained** — CUSTODY REGAINED on SIM-DRO-01: cloud sigma_pos 0.4 km < 100 km after 5 space-observer tracklet(s) (1.0 h after loss, 11.5 h after the burn).
- `2026-02-25T22:00:00Z` **maneuver_characterised** — MANEUVER CHARACTERISED: dv 30.02 +/- 0.03 m/s (truth 30 m/s, error +0.07 %), direction +/- 0.06 deg (0.11 deg from truth), RTN -29.6/+5.1/-1.3 m/s, epoch 2026-02-25T08:30:45Z +/- 53 s (+45 s from truth); radial (inward).
- `2026-02-25T22:00:01Z` **brief_ready** — Analyst brief generated (SIMULATED — notional actor).
- `2026-02-26T17:00:00Z` **entered_region** — [SIMULATED truth] SIM-DRO-01 enters L1 gateway (17,690 km from L1); custody status at the time: CUSTODY.

## Maneuver characterisation
- Δv magnitude: **30.02 ± 0.03 m/s** (1-sigma). SIMULATED truth: 30.00 m/s → error 0.1 %.
- Direction (1-sigma 0.1°; 0.1° from truth), moon-centred frames:
  - RTN (radial / transverse ≈ along-track / normal): -29.6 / 5.1 / -1.3 m/s (truth -29.6 / 5.0 / -1.3).
  - VNB (velocity / normal / bi-normal): 13.2 / -1.3 / -26.9 m/s (truth 13.1 / -1.3 / -26.9).
- Burn epoch: **2026-02-25T08:30:45Z ± 53 s** (truth 2026-02-25T08:30:00Z, error 45 s); the burn is only known to lie between the last pre-burn tracklet and the flagged one.
- Fit: 10 post-burn angle pairs, residual RMS 1.00 arcsec, reduced chi-square 1.23, converged: True.
- Descriptive classification (heuristic, no intent): radial (inward); dominant component in moon-centred RTN: R=-0.98 T=+0.17 N=-0.04; Jacobi constant decreased (energy added in the rotating frame); post-burn energy allows Earth-Moon transit through both gateways; Earth-relative energy increased (outward / apogee raise).

## Custody status
- Over the 145 hourly frames SIM-DRO-01 was in CUSTODY 135 h, DEGRADED 9 h, LOST 1 h (93.1 % custody). Thresholds on the particle-cloud position sigma: < 100 km CUSTODY, > 1,000 km LOST.
- Position sigma at detection 104 km; peak 1,053 km at 2026-02-25T19:00:00Z; after regain 0.4 km.
- Loss mechanism: lunar glare (the object was too close to the bright Moon on the sky) (79 of 86 blind hours after the detection; in the other 7 hours no site had the object above its elevation limit at night, which is not a glare effect). At the loss epoch the blocker was lunar glare; Moon 64 % illuminated and the object 8.9° from it on the sky. Hourly blind-reason counts between detection and loss: no_site_available ×5, moon_exclusion ×4; detection to end of window: no_site_available ×7, moon_exclusion ×79.
- Observations used: 54 (15 ground pre-burn, 1 ground post-burn, 38 space-observer follow-ups); by sensor: haleakala 5, teide 4, socorro 4, siding_spring 2, diego_garcia 1, dro_obs 9, geo_east 2, geo_west 4, l1_halo_obs 15, nrho_obs 8.
- Other catalogued SIMULATED objects (space-observer tasking, linear covariance): lowest custody SIM-XGEO-DEBRIS-01 83 %, SIM-DRO-02 100 %, SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01 100 %.

## Reachability (where it could be — awareness and traffic safety only)
- Computed from the last good estimate (2026-02-25T08:00:00Z) with an **assumed** 100 m/s budget over 168 h: 1728 sampled impulsive burns (96 directions × magnitude ladder × 3 burn epochs spanning the detection gap).
- the Earth-Moon L1 gateway (the low-energy doorway between Earth space and the lunar vicinity): already on the unperturbed path (first entry +34 h with no burn; earliest +29 h over the sampled burns).
- the Earth-Moon L2 gateway (the doorway to the lunar far side and translunar space): 27.8 % of sampled rays, earliest arrival +108 h, minimum Δv to reach ≈ 11 m/s.
- Not reachable within budget and horizon: the 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) corridor used by the notional allied relay; the lunar south-pole approach volume; the low-lunar-orbit shell (below 5 000 km altitude); low lunar orbit below 500 km; a return path toward the geostationary (GEO) belt; the exterior realm beyond the L2 neck (outside the volume Moon-pointed sensors search); the lunar surface (impact).
- SIMULATED truth for reference: closest approach to L1 508 km at 2026-02-27T02:00:00Z; closest approach to SIM-NRHO-RELAY-01 56,192 km at 2026-02-27T02:00:00Z.

## Sensor tasking actions
- geo_west redirected at 2026-02-25T20:00:00Z to RA 81.59°, Dec 28.33° (centroid of the reachable set as seen from the sensor), 1 field(s) searched (mosaic radius 1.50°; 1 would cover the full 90th-percentile spread of 0.55°); the SIMULATED truth was 0.20° from the boresight at range 328,193 km, predicted magnitude 16.9.
- Also tasked in the same slot and verified against truth: geo_east (1 of 1 field(s), p90 spread 0.54°, range 330,367 km, truth 0.21° from boresight, magnitude 17.3); l1_halo_obs (25 of 73 field(s), p90 spread 8.49°, range 18,518 km, truth 2.52° from boresight, magnitude 13.3); dro_obs (13 of 13 field(s), p90 spread 3.47°, range 52,383 km, truth 1.06° from boresight, magnitude 12.4); nrho_obs (4 of 4 field(s), p90 spread 1.79°, range 99,261 km, truth 0.55° from boresight, magnitude 16.4).
- Not tasked: l2_halo_obs — solar exclusion.
- Scheduler: greedy (logdet gain, FOV acquisition model), priority 3 on the object of interest, search budget 25 fields per slot (shared by the scheduler's acquisition model and the truth verification), 1.0 h re-planning latency; 38 follow-up tracklets at the follow-up cadence; 5 tasked look(s) evaluated against truth.
- Routine schedule segment A: 10 objects, 6 space observers, 407 looks over 68 h, custody 100 %, mean time since last observation 4.6 h.
- Routine schedule segment B: 11 objects, 6 space observers, 288 looks over 48 h, custody 100 %, mean time since last observation 3.7 h.
- Routine schedule segment C: 11 objects, 6 space observers, 168 looks over 28 h, custody 92 %, mean time since last observation 3.1 h.

## Confidence and caveats
- Detection test: per-update NIS against a chi-square threshold with per-test false-alarm probability alpha = 0.01 (family-wise over the run: NIS threshold 18.3); 49 of 54 updates tested, run status 'maneuver_declared'.
- Covariance realism (simulation-only, needs truth): mean normalised estimation error squared (NEES) 4.52 over 52 epochs against the 95 % band [5.10, 6.98] for 6 degrees of freedom → below the band: the covariance is conservative (larger than the realised errors), which is safe for custody but overstates the uncertainty; baseline (pre-burn) mean NEES 0.84 vs the over-confidence bound 14.10. Successive errors of one run are correlated, so the band is indicative; the Monte-Carlo NEES study lives in the OD module's tests.
- After the detection the filter prior was re-opened for an impulsive Δv of 1-sigma 25 m/s at an unknown epoch in the last gap; this assumption must bound the burn class or the filter would be over-confident.
- Reachability fractions are fractions of sampled (direction, epoch) rays under an assumed budget; they are not probabilities of any action and assert no intent.
- Assumption: All sensors are notional (assumed representative specs); astrometric noise 1 arcsec (1-sigma, isotropic on-sky).
- Assumption: Routine custody: one ground tracklet every 2 h when any site can see the object; space observers are allocated to the libration-point objects until the tasker escalates.
- Assumption: Filter: UKF with DE440s Earth+Moon+Sun+SRP dynamics, process-noise PSD 1e-18 km^2/s^3; the t0 prior (5 km / 0.2 m/s, 1-sigma) stands for the catalogue covariance of an object that has been under custody for weeks (the 20 km / 2 m/s acquisition prior would drift past 100 km in the 8-h gaps between ground sites); after a gross NIS exceedance the prior is re-opened for an impulsive dv of sigma 25 m/s at an unknown epoch in the last gap (must bound the burn class).
- Assumption: Custody thresholds on the particle-cloud RSS position sigma: < 100 km CUSTODY, 100-1000 km DEGRADED, > 1000 km LOST.
- Assumption: Reachability: assumed 100 m/s planning budget, 168 h horizon, impulsive burns on a Fibonacci sphere x absolute magnitude ladder x burn epochs spanning the detection gap; fractions are fractions of sampled (direction, epoch) rays.
- Assumption: Tasking: greedy scheduler (trace gain for routine custody, log-det information gain for the escalation because re-acquisition must resolve range and velocity, not just plane-of-sky position) with the FOV acquisition model; every tasked look is verified against the SIMULATED truth (visibility model + mosaic of fields around the reachable-set centroid), never assumed; the scheduler's acquisition model and the verification share one search budget of 25 fields per 60-min slot (no explicit slew/exposure timeline); one slot of re-planning latency between the loss declaration and the first tasked look.
- Assumption: Ground-blind attribution: per hourly frame only the sites that are available (astronomical night, object above the minimum elevation) are asked why they are blocked; frames where no site is available are reported as 'no_site_available', not as glare.
- Assumption: Force model has no lunar gravity field or planetary perturbations beyond the Sun; light-time and aberration are not modelled.
